answer.reason: Several events of the story took place at the brook Kidron, so a short line of its chief events is warranted.

clauses.english: was crossed by King David and all the people toward the wilderness
clauses.quote: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron

clauses.english: was where Josiah burned the grove and stamped it to powder
clauses.quote: burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder

clauses.english: was crossed by Jesus and his disciples on the way to a garden
clauses.quote: he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron

doubts: Other burnings and castings into Kidron (Asa's idol, Hezekiah's uncleanness and altars, Josiah's altar dust) are omitted as less chief than Josiah's burning of the grove.
2CH 33:14 is marked but speaks of a wall in the valley, not of Kidron's own events, so it is left out.
NEH 2:15 says only 'the brook' and 1KI 2:37 is a warning to Shimei, not an event, so neither is used.
